findings.source_quote: καὶ ὡς ἰδίᾳ χαριζόμενος ἐπιθυμίᾳ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ βούλησιν ἐκτελεῖ
findings.english_quote: and, while gratifying his own desire, carries out God’s will.
findings.issue: The merely temporal “while” does not adequately preserve the characterization marked by ὡς with the participle. It also obscures the parallel with καὶ αὐτὸς δὲ ὡς ἑαυτῷ χαριζόμενος, rendered later as “and he too, as though gratifying himself.” The Greek need not imply that gratification is unreal, but both constructions expressly present the action under the description of self-gratification.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the source-transparent rendering “and, as one gratifying his own desire, carries out God’s will,” with a corresponding treatment of the later construction: “and he too, as one gratifying himself, offers God thanks for them.” Explain in a note whether ὡς is understood as subjective characterization or as “as though”; do not imply that the latter necessarily denies actual gratification. Any revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: παρὰ δὲ τὸ μέτρον ἐξελθὼν καὶ ἑαυτῷ τὴν κρίσιν λαβὼν ἀσεβεῖ.
findings.english_quote: but one who goes beyond the proper measure and takes judgment upon himself acts impiously.
findings.issue: The main English can preserve the ambiguity, but the lexical note presents assuming authority to judge or punish as the meaning without acknowledging the materially different possibility of receiving or incurring judgment for oneself. The preceding discussion of being judged and punished makes that alternative contextually viable. This is an interpretive-disclosure issue, not a defect requiring verification of the already checked print.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to distinguish “takes judgment into his own hands” from “incurs judgment for himself,” explaining why the former was chosen while preserving the latter. The present main wording may remain as an intentionally ambiguous rendering if the note explicitly identifies both readings; otherwise choose defensible, clearer wording and submit it for fresh review.
